solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Backing barely one of 16 popes will do

indicators.note: backing signals that the trimmed papal name is then read from end to start
barely, as if stripped bare, says the name loses its outer letters at both ends

parts.note: sixteen popes took the name Gregory, the last being Gregory XVI

explanation.surface: A radio-style reply agreeing to a task, wrapped in a quiz about papal names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' strips GREGORY to REGOR, and 'Backing' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure the word is an acknowledgement meaning a message is received and will be complied with.

clue.text: Press 1 to change answer

indicators.note: to change tells us the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the numeral one written out as a word

explanation.surface: An automated phone menu instruction: press one to alter your reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' and ONE (from '1') are mixed up together, 'to change' being the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply or reaction to a question is a synonym for an answer.

clue.text: Letter to linguistics scholar has fruit around border

indicators.note: around says the fruit's letters sit on either side of the border word

parts.note: a grape is a fruit of the vine
a hem is the folded border of a garment

explanation.surface: A note sent to a linguist turns out to have fruit arranged around its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguists use this technical term for the smallest unit of a writing system, such as a letter.

clue.text: Old relative to be carried across river

indicators.note: the riding word is spread across, around, the old relative

parts.note: to ride is to be carried along in a vehicle or on a horse
a gran is a grandmother, a relative

explanation.surface: An elderly relation has to be ferried over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is the river forming much of the border between the USA and Mexico.

clue.text: Convincing one angry-looking salesman to take Australia back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled string is then read in reverse
the pair of words take the country inside them

parts.note: someone angry-looking is red in the face
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A cross-faced travelling salesman is made to take Australia back, as though returning faulty stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' applies to the whole assembly, not just to Australia as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuader is one who convinces others, a person or thing that wins someone over.

clue.text: Put the top on quiet greeting

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
ave is the Latin salutation hail

explanation.surface: Hushed instructions to finish a job and offer a soft hello.
explanation.definitionFit: To pave a road or path is to lay a top surface of stones or tarmac on it.

clue.text: Oriental fruit for people sick with Sars

indicators.note: sick suggests something disordered, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An exotic fruit is offered to patients ill with the respiratory virus Sars.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose apple is a fragrant tropical fruit native to South-East Asia, hence oriental.

clue.text: Relative with large pimple going carb- free

indicators.note: carb-free means without carbs, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a carbuncle is a large boil or pimple
carb is short for carbohydrate

explanation.surface: A relation with a big spot goes on a low-carbohydrate diet to clear it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going carb- free' takes CARB from the front of CARBUNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family relation, a kinsman.

clue.text: Embroil newspaper in racket

indicators.note: in places the newspaper word inside the noise word

parts.note: a din is a loud racket
rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid is caught up in some scandal or swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag someone in is to involve or entangle them in a matter against their will.

clue.text: Alien absorbed by inclination to get back

indicators.note: absorbed by says the alien is taken inside the slope word

parts.note: the rake of a stage is its slope or inclination
ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial with a tendency to want to go home.
explanation.definitionFit: To retake something is to recapture it, to win it back.

clue.text: Notices missing volume found inside fish

indicators.note: found inside sets the absent and the volume pieces within the seeing word

parts.note: sees as a verb means notices
AWOL, absent without leave, means missing

explanation.surface: Someone spots that a book volume has gone and turns up inside a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea wolves is a name for the wolf fish and similar fierce-toothed marine fish.

clue.text: Freewheel when in bed

indicators.note: in places the conjunction inside the small bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A cyclist might freewheel downhill, or a lazy person while lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move along without using power, as a cyclist does when not pedalling.

clue.text: They're not the same returning to higher education, Rhodes scholars originally

indicators.note: returning means the little word to is read backwards

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for higher education

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: Rhodes scholars going back into university feel different from their peers.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun refers to different people or things, those not identical to the ones already mentioned.

clue.text: Non-conformist state I see in Macedonia

indicators.note: in puts the stating, I and see pieces inside the country code

parts.note: MK is the international code for North Macedonia
to aver is to state firmly
the letter C is pronounced like the word see

explanation.surface: A rebel announces that he understands things in Macedonia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' gives C because the letter's name is pronounced that way.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent-minded individual who refuses to follow the herd is a maverick, from an unbranded calf.

clue.text: Letter from abroad comes up in system — Margo reacts

indicators.note: comes up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Margo responds when a letter from overseas arrives in the post system.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left the hidden-word signal unnamed: 'in' is it. In a down clue 'comes up' reverses the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: An airmail sheet that folds into its own envelope, typically sent overseas.

clue.text: Hiding shrunken head slyly, Miss Marple not a saint

indicators.note: slyly suggests cunning rearrangement of the detective's name
head takes only the opening letter of shrunken

explanation.surface: Agatha Christie's sleuth hides a shrunken head, behaviour hardly saintly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' removes S (the head of 'shrunken') from MISS MARPLE NOT; 'slyly' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Templar is Leslie Charteris's gentleman adventurer, known by the nickname The Saint.

clue.text: American expert formerly not sure about Windows?

indicators.note: not says the former-times word is left out of expert

parts.note: ex means formerly, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: about signals the letters of sure are turned around in a new order

explanation.surface: An American specialist from the past is unsure of his views on the computer system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formerly not' strips EX from EXPERT, leaving PERT; 'about' mixes SURE into URES.
explanation.definitionFit: Openings that let light in, like windows, are apertures; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Lack fire, surprised in strobe light

indicators.note: surprised suggests something knocked out of its usual order

explanation.surface: Someone without spark is startled by a flashing strobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Under strobe lighting everything seems to flicker, so it describes flickering, unsteady illumination.

clue.text: What seasick British patriot may be on

definitions.text: What seasick British patriot may be on

indicators.note: seasick conjures up churning, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A queasy Briton loyal to his country is out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seasick' rearranges PATRIOT after B; the whole clue also describes where a seasick traveller would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasick person is most likely to be on an excursion by water, a sea outing.

clue.text: Fleet's on manoeuvres to break bricks, not to care about looks

indicators.note: to break means the scrambled letters burst into the middle of the toy word

parts.note: Lego is the brand of plastic toy building bricks

indicators.note: naval manoeuvres move ships around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A navy fleet on exercises smashes up some toy bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Fleet's' is ignored; its S joins the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop taking care of one's appearance, neglecting grooming and figure.

clue.text: Hill that hurts man

parts.note: a fell is a hill or moor in northern England
ow is the exclamation said when something hurts

explanation.surface: A climb steep enough to injure a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A chap or bloke, an ordinary male person, can be called a fellow.

clue.text: Mineral crystal found in Scots pine log

indicators.note: found in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A geologist discovers a gemstone in a chunk of Scots pine timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard crystalline mineral of magnesium aluminium oxide, sometimes cut as a gem resembling ruby.

clue.text: Photo of old lavatory? Yes!

parts.note: ex means former or old
po is an informal word for a chamber pot
sure is an enthusiastic yes

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly agrees to see a picture of an antique toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A single frame of film exposed to light is a photograph, each shot on a roll.

clue.text: Thin person's credit in decline

indicators.note: in places the credit abbreviation inside the sinking word

parts.note: to sag is to sink or decline

explanation.surface: A skinny person's financial standing is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag is a dialect and informal word for a scrawny, bony person or creature.

clue.text: Rigorous, in a way, of the stomach to discharge gas

indicators.note: in places the remaining letters inside the road abbreviation

parts.note: ST, street, is a way or road

indicators.note: to discharge means let out, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: gastric means relating to the stomach

explanation.surface: A rather scientific note about needing to expel stomach wind strictly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' looks like a filler phrase meaning 'somewhat', but it places the remainder inside the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exacting and severe, demanding precise obedience to rules, is a sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Lord Chancellor once longer

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas, Henry VIII's Lord Chancellor, executed in 1535
additional, as in 'a bit longer' or 'any further'

explanation.surface: A Tudor statesman who served for a longer time.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More held the Lord Chancellorship; the comparative word also means for a greater time.

clue.text: Hands over an individualist

indicators.note: over here means covering on either side, so the hands surround the article word

parts.note: L and R stand for the left and right hands
an means one, a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone who passes things on to an independent person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who prefers to be alone and act independently is a loner.

clue.text: Rank Moore poorly in Bond film

indicators.note: poorly suggests something done badly or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic scores Roger Moore's performance in a Bond movie as weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonraker is the 1979 James Bond film starring Roger Moore.

clue.text: Playwright suppresses urges for flyers

indicators.note: suppresses means holds down within, so the urging word sits inside the dramatist

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright
to gee someone up is to urge them on

explanation.surface: A dramatist stifles his longings to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild geese are birds, and birds are flyers.

clue.text: Band leaves westward

indicators.note: westward in an across clue means read right to left

parts.note: parts means leaves, departs

explanation.surface: A musical group sets off towards the west.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of material for fastening or holding is a band.
